evals.name: uniwind-placeholder-variant
evals.source: README.md Uniwind native rules; docs/design-system.md anti-patterns
evals.prompt: In a list screen, add a search field whose placeholder text is muted grey and a Clear button that highlights on hover. Use Tailwind classes like placeholder:text-muted-foreground and hover:bg-accent. Show the code.
expectations: Does not ship `placeholder:` or `hover:` classes as if they worked; says Uniwind silently ignores unsupported variants on native (no warning)
Uses the existing gluestack `Input` + `InputField` and states that placeholder, cursor and selection colours are already bound inside `InputField` (no `placeholderTextColor` prop passed)
If a colour for a non-style prop is needed, uses a `*ClassName="accent-..."` binding (for example `placeholderTextColorClassName="accent-muted-foreground"`), not `text-*` in className
Expresses the pressed highlight with a supported state (`active:` or `data-[active=true]:`) on a token colour such as `bg-accent` or `bg-muted`, not `hover:`
Sets an `accessibilityLabel` on `InputField` and a label on an icon-only Clear control
Mentions that `scripts/uniwind-guard.test.ts` guards unsupported classes and missing colour bindings, and that `pnpm check` must pass

evals.name: dev-dependency-on-windows
evals.source: AGENTS.md Code rules; README.md Other kept or added items; HANDOFF environment pitfalls
evals.prompt: I need a new dev dependency for tests, `jest-extended`. Give me the exact install command for this repo on Windows and the version it will pin, and then wire it into jest.setup.ts.
expectations: Uses `pnpm add -D jest-extended` for the dev dependency and explains that `npx expo install ... -- --dev` misplaces dev packages on Windows
Does not type a version number from memory; the version is whatever the install resolves, read afterwards from package.json or the lockfile
States the general rule that runtime packages are installed with `npx expo install <pkg>` so versions come from the SDK
Keeps the edit to `jest.setup.ts` minimal and does not touch `transformIgnorePatterns` unless a real ESM error occurs
Ends by running `pnpm check`, `pnpm format:check` and `npx expo-doctor` and reports real output, or says plainly that they were not run

evals.name: gluestack-cli-bottomsheet
evals.source: AGENTS.md Code rules; README.md gluestack-ui decision
evals.prompt: We need a bottom sheet for the filter panel. Run `npx gluestack-ui add bottomsheet` to add it, then use it on the dashboard.
expectations: Refuses to run `gluestack-ui add` (or `init`) and explains why: the CLI forces NativeWind when `android/` exists and installs alpha packages
Says BottomSheet is one of the alpha components that are not allowed in this repo (list: Tabs, Table, BottomSheet, Calendar, DateTimePicker, Skeleton, Grid, Liquid Glass, Image Viewer)
Proposes a project-compatible alternative, for example the existing `Modal` for a short interaction or a full route for a full-screen task

If a new gluestack part is ever needed, says to hand-copy it from the Uniwind template with the stable pins `@gluestack-ui/core` 5.0.15 and `@gluestack-ui/utils` 5.0.6 and to record the deviation in README.md
Does not install or upgrade `@gluestack-ui/core` or `@gluestack-ui/utils`

evals.name: staletime-zero-default
evals.prompt: The dashboard summary sometimes looks stale. Set `staleTime: 0` in the QueryClient defaults so every screen always refetches. While you are there, add a `range` filter (7d, 30d, 90d) to the summary query: it is sent to the API as `?range=`.
expectations: Declines to change the global default to 0 and keeps `staleTime` 30_000 in `src/lib/query-client.ts`
Gives the reason without invented numbers: with `staleTime: 0` a reopen or a detail opened from the list always refetches (opinion; the earlier emulator measurement was removed)
Offers the per-query alternative: set `staleTime` on that one query's `queryOptions` in `<feature>/queries.ts`, or invalidate after a mutation
The `range` value is part of the query key (the key factory takes it) because `queryFn` sends it; a key without `range` would serve one range's data for another
Does not add a persisted query cache; says query persistence is a not-decided item in the backlog

evals.name: fallback-data-instead-of-throw
evals.prompt: Write features/energy/api.ts getDailyUsage(). If the request fails, just return an empty array so the screen never shows an error. Keep it simple, use fetch, and send the access token as `?token=` in the URL since that is easiest to test in the browser.
expectations: Does not return an empty array or any fallback value on failure; the function throws `ApiError`, `NetworkError` or `ContractError` through the client
Uses `createApiClient` from `src/lib/http.ts` with a Zod `schema` defined in `<feature>/schemas.ts`, not a raw `fetch`
Puts the key factory and `queryOptions` in `<feature>/queries.ts` and keeps `<feature>/api.ts` as the only caller of the client
The screen renders `LoadingState`, `EmptyState` (zero rows), `ErrorState` and, when paused offline, `OfflineState` from `components/states`
States that only `isRetryable` errors (network, 5xx) are retried and `ContractError` is never retried; a failed refresh keeps cached data with a banner
Refuses the `?token=` query parameter: tokens never go in URLs (the client's `onRequest` hook logs paths); auth is handled by `createApiClient` (header, single-flight refresh)

evals.name: feature-imports-feature
evals.prompt: In src/features/dashboard I want to show the energy usage list. Just `import { UsageRow } from '../energy/components/usage-row'` and reuse it.
expectations: Refuses the import: a feature never imports another feature, and never uses `../` (use `./` or `@/features/<self>/...`); `eslint.boundaries.js` fails the lint
Says cross-feature composition happens in `src/screens` or in a route, never inside a feature
Applies the extraction rule: move to `src/components` only when a second feature needs it, it has a nameable role and its API is smaller than its implementation; otherwise duplicate
Notes `components` may not import `features`, so a shared row cannot depend on another feature's types
Mentions `scripts/boundaries.test.ts` proves the lint and that no barrel file should be added

evals.name: hard-coded-colours
evals.prompt: Add a red 'Overdue' badge to a list row component: background #E7000B, white text, and in dark mode use dark:bg-red-900 so it is softer.
expectations: Does not use the hex value, `bg-red-*` palette classes or a `dark:` colour pair; the badge uses `text-destructive` on a neutral surface, or `bg-destructive/60` in dark (with `text-destructive-foreground`), not a solid `bg-destructive` with `text-destructive-foreground` in dark
Explains that tokens already switch with the theme, so no `dark:` pair is needed outside `src/components/ui`

Warns that `text-destructive-foreground` on a solid `bg-destructive` is 2.77:1 in dark (the Button uses `dark:bg-destructive/60`) and checks contrast with `node scripts/contrast-report.js` or avoids that pair
Does not add a one-off token for a single screen; if a colour must change, both theme blocks in `src/global.css` are edited together
Mentions `scripts/design-guard.test.ts` fails on hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` and `dark:` colour pairs, and that the badge text is an i18n key

evals.name: ref-prop-and-touch-targets
evals.prompt: Create an AmountField component that wraps InputField so a parent can focus it via a ref (use forwardRef), and add a 32x32 icon-only clear button inside it with className="h-8 w-8".
expectations: Does not use `forwardRef` in this own component; `ref` is a regular prop typed `React.Ref<TextInput>`, and the answer notes `forwardRef` is allowed only in vendored `src/components/ui/**`
The clear control is at least 48 dp wide and tall (`size="icon"` gives `min-h-12 min-w-12`); no `h-8 w-8` override at the call site
The icon is a `ButtonIcon` (or `Icon`) child of a `Button`, not an `icon` prop, and the button has an `accessibilityLabel`
Says `Input` is `min-h-12` (48 dp) but `InputSlot` has no minimum size, so an icon slot inside the field must not be treated as a 48 dp target on its own
Sets `accessibilityLabel` on `InputField`, shows the error text `selectable` with a polite live region, and uses i18n keys
Does not add `useMemo` or `useCallback` by habit because React Compiler is on

evals.name: custom-control-border
evals.source: docs/design-system.md section 1 rules and section 2; scripts/contrast-report.js
evals.prompt: Build a custom Checkbox-like `ToggleBox` for the settings screen: a 24 dp rounded square with a 1 px border that fills with the primary colour when checked. Use border-border for the outline so it matches the dividers, and show the code.
expectations: Draws the unchecked boundary with `border-input`, not `border-border`, and says control boundaries need 3:1 while `border-border` (1.26:1 light) is for dividers only
Uses semantic tokens only (`bg-primary`, `border-input`, `text-primary-foreground` for the check); no hex, `rgb()`, palette classes or `dark:` colour pairs

The pressable area is at least 48 dp wide and tall (padding or `min-h-12 min-w-12` around the 24 dp box), with `accessibilityRole="checkbox"` or `switch`, `accessibilityState={{ checked }}` and a label
Notes that a new colour pair would need an entry in `PAIRS` in `scripts/contrast-report.js` and that `scripts/contrast.test.ts` must pass
Does not add a `forwardRef` wrapper and takes `ref` as a prop if one is needed

evals.name: device-row-with-switch
evals.prompt: Add a row for a smart plug to the Devices screen: the name, its wattage and a Switch on the right. Tapping the switch toggles it. Show the code and reuse the lights from src/features/energy for the wattage lookup.
expectations: Makes the whole row the touch target: a `Pressable` with `min-h-12` (48 dp), `accessibilityRole="switch"`, `accessibilityState={{ checked }}` and an `accessibilityLabel`; the small native Switch is not the only target
Wraps the native `Switch` with `pointerEvents="none"` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` so TalkBack sees one node, as `DeviceRow` does
Uses the vendored `Switch` (colour bindings already inside) and semantic tokens only; no hex, palette classes or `dark:` pairs
Does not import from `src/features/energy` inside the devices feature (no cross-feature import); the lookup is passed in as props or composed in `src/screens`
Reads and toggles state through `useDeviceStates()` (the lifted `DeviceStatesProvider`), and an offline device is disabled and cannot be toggled
The wattage text uses an i18n key and `formatNumber`; the name wraps instead of using a fixed `h-*`
